meta.title: SF Bay Area Appraisal Association | Antiques, Art & Collectibles
meta.description: SF Bay Area Appraisal Association (in formation): collecting antiques, art and collectibles of every kind in the Bay Area, including Asian art, hardwood furniture, painting, jewelry and watches, trading cards, mid-century design and European and American decorative arts, with appraisal and valuation advice.

status: The association is being formed: we are recruiting our first appraisers and partner institutions, and bookings open soon.

home.eyebrow: San Francisco Bay Area · Antiques, art and collectibles
home.title: Antiques, art and collectibles, collected in the Bay Area
home.lead: We collect from Bay Area collectors across every region and category: Asian art, hardwood furniture, painting, jewelry and watches, trading cards, mid-century design, European and American decorative arts and more. Each object is registered, photographed and given a first appraisal, then shown here and offered at auction.
home.heroCaption: Jar with dragon, Ming dynasty, Xuande period. The Metropolitan Museum of Art (CC0), for illustration only
home.collectionLead: Public museum objects, each with notes on what an appraiser looks at.
home.step1Text: Front, back, base, marks and any damage, with dimensions and what you know of its history.
home.step2Text: A first opinion from the photos, and whether we need to see it in person.
home.step3Text: Estimate, reserve, fees and settlement are agreed in writing before we take the object.
home.step4Text: The object gets a number and catalogue photos, appears here and goes to auction.
home.pricingLead: A written quote by number of items, category and purpose before any work; never a percentage of value, and the conclusion does not change the fee.

home.itemsEmpty: Our first objects are being registered and will appear here soon.

services.title: Services
services.lead: Appraisals by category and purpose. Each purpose calls for a different type of value and report.
services.ceramicsText: Imperial and private-kiln wares of every period: blue-and-white, famille rose, monochromes, Song celadons and Jun ware.
services.jadeText: Archaic and Ming–Qing jade, jadeite, gemstones and jewelry, with instrument testing where needed.
services.paintingText: Hanging scrolls, handscrolls, albums and fans: brushwork, inscriptions, seals, records and mounting.
services.bronzeText: Ritual bronzes, gilt-bronze Buddhist figures, gold and silver, and cloisonné.
services.furnitureText: Huanghuali, zitan and other hardwood furniture and scholar's objects: timber, construction and replaced parts.
services.consultingText: Inventories, care and storage, and preparing a collection for sale or donation.
services.insuranceText: Replacement value, for coverage, schedule updates and claims.
services.estateText: Fair market value. A non-cash donation deduction over $5,000 (per item or group of similar items) requires a qualified appraisal by a qualified appraiser and a signed IRS Form 8283, Section B.
services.divisionText: For divorce, inheritance or partners dividing assets.
services.saleText: Authenticity and market opinion before you sell, consign to auction or buy.
services.deliverable2: Material, technique, marks and condition, including restoration
services.deliverable4: Type of value, effective date and limiting conditions
services.standardsText: The association will require every appraiser to write appraisal reports under the Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice (USPAP); not to buy or sell objects they appraise, and to disclose any interest in the client or the object; and to state plainly where the evidence is inconclusive instead of going beyond it. Each appraiser's background and credentials will be published when bookings open.

collection.title: Reference catalogue
collection.lead: Every object below is in the public collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art; none was appraised or is owned by us. For each we list the date and material, and what an appraiser usually examines on this kind of piece, for collectors to learn from.
collection.disclaimer: Every object here is in a public museum collection. Images and data are used under The Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access (CC0) for study and teaching. We have not appraised these objects, and nothing here is a market valuation.

pricing.title: Fees
pricing.lead: Estimated fee ranges while the association is being formed; they may change before bookings open. Fees are confirmed in writing before any work starts and depend on the object, the research needed and the purpose of the report.
pricing.consultationDesc: 30 minutes to discuss your objects and needs, and whether we need to see them in person.
pricing.singleItemDesc: A full report on one object, including research and documentation.
pricing.multipleItemsDesc: A reduced rate per item when appraised in one visit.
pricing.collectionDesc: Inventory and appraisal of 10 or more items.
pricing.specializedDesc: Archaic jade, bronzes, major paintings and other objects that need deep research or instrument testing.
pricing.insuranceDesc: A written replacement-value report for coverage and claims.
pricing.note1: We never charge a percentage of value, and the conclusion does not change the fee.
pricing.note2: Instrument tests (such as XRF composition analysis or thermoluminescence dating) are done by an independent laboratory, quoted separately in advance.
pricing.note3: Home visits within the Bay Area carry a travel charge.

contact.title: Booking: opening soon

asian.name: Chinese and Asian art
asian.why: The largest collecting category in the Bay Area.
asian.what: Ceramics (imperial, private-kiln and Song wares), jade and hardstone, painting and calligraphy, bronzes and Buddhist sculpture, scholar's objects and snuff bottles, Japanese and Korean art
asian.prep: Clear photos (including the base and any marks), dimensions, purchase or family records
asian.limit: Archaeological objects need documented lawful provenance and export

furniture.name: Hardwood furniture
furniture.what: Huanghuali, zitan and other hardwood furniture, plus brush pots, boxes and other wooden scholar's objects
furniture.prep: Overall and joinery photos, dimensions, any replaced or repaired parts
furniture.limit: Regulated timbers need full provenance documents

cards.name: Trading cards
cards.why: Large card shows run in the Bay Area almost every month.
cards.what: Graded, slabbed sports cards, Pokémon, Magic: The Gathering, One Piece and more; Chinese- and Japanese-language cards welcome
cards.prep: Grading company, grade and certificate number; front and back photos of the slab
cards.limit: No ungraded cards or sealed packs for now

jewelry.name: Jewelry and watches
jewelry.why: The most common category in estate clear-outs, and quick to sell.
jewelry.what: Signed jewelry, coloured gemstones, diamonds, gold, mechanical watches
jewelry.prep: Lab certificates, original receipts, boxes and papers

california.name: Painting
california.why: Strong local demand, with California schools especially active.
california.what: Oils, watercolours, prints and drawings, including California Impressionism (plein air), Bay Area Figurative and contemporary works
california.prep: Front and back photos (including labels and inscriptions), dimensions, exhibition or publication history

design.name: Mid-century modern design
design.why: The Bay Area has a strong design tradition.
design.prep: Photos of makers' marks and signatures

western.name: European and American furniture and decorative arts
western.what: Furniture, silver, porcelain, glass and textiles

collecting.title: What we collect
collecting.lead: We collect objects of every kind, from any region. These are the seven main categories of the Bay Area market; anything outside them is welcome too.
collecting.never: In every category we do not accept ivory or rhino horn, archaeological objects without lawful provenance, or counterfeits.
